## $x_1$-wall corner refresh inside tangential ghost slabs {#sec-ch03-cornerrefresh}

<!-- PROVENANCE

sources: src/mesh/meshblock.cpp, src/bc/bc_func.hpp, src/mesh/mesh.cpp, tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp
status: draft
-->

### Summary

The tangential exchange fills the $x_2$ and $x_3$ ghost slabs with the neighbour's interior, but within those slabs the
$x_1$ ghost rows (the corners next to an $x_1$ wall) hold whatever the neighbour's wall wrote last, or stale values on
a periodic edge. A stencil with cross-derivatives, such as viscosity next to the wall, then reads a wall corner that
does not belong to this column. Re-applying the $x_1$ boundary function on the slabs makes those corners the wall
ghosts of the updated slab.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** After the tangential exchange, each installed $x_1$ boundary function except outflow is applied again inside
the $x_2$ and $x_3$ ghost slabs (a `reflecting` wall on a block with no physical tangential face: once over the whole
array), so the ghost corners next to an $x_1$ wall match the updated column; a rule, stated in the Derivation layer.

**Data.** In/out: the ghost corner cells of the conserved (`hydro_u`) and scalar (`scalar_s`) arrays, in their own units.

**Placement.** End of every per-stage block sync, after the tangential exchange.

**Activation.** No switch; always on in the block's per-stage sync; not done by `Mesh::exchange_ghost_zones`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact, provided each boundary function gives the same ghosts when called again on an
$n_g$-wide slab.

**Evidence.** `test_wb_wall_corner` (Cartesian only; untested on the cubed sphere and on spherical-polar); check
`[C19]`; the ctest entry was not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).
:::

Local symbols: $n_{\mathrm t}$ the array length along a tangential direction, ghosts
included (count); $n_{\mathrm{slab}} = \min(n_g, \lfloor n_{\mathrm t}/2\rfloor)$ the width of each end slab the
refresh rewrites (count).

### Derivation

There is nothing to derive; it is a consistency rule. For each installed $x_1$ bfunc that is not outflow, and each
tangential direction with more than one cell, the bfunc is called on the first and last $n_{\mathrm{slab}}$ cells of
that direction, with $n_{\mathrm t}$ and $n_{\mathrm{slab}}$ as above (`int g = ng < n / 2 ? ng : n / 2` in {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}), unless that tangential face is itself physical and not periodic, in which case its own bfunc already
wrote the corner. A `reflecting` $x_1$ wall on a block none of whose tangential faces is physical is instead called
once over the whole array: it mirrors each $x_1$ row from that row's own interior, so the one call writes the same
corner values as the slab calls and rewrites the other $x_1$ ghost rows with the bits they already hold. The rule relies on the contract stated with the `BC_FUNCTION` macro: a face function called again on
a tangential slab must not depend on the slab's size and must give the same ghosts ({{< code src/bc/bc_func.hpp BC_FUNCTION >}}).
Outflow is excluded because its background must match the whole block and it needs primitives.

**What `physical` resolves to on each layout**, because the rule reads the installed functions and the layouts do
not install the same ones. On `slab` and `cubed`, construction removes the $x_2$ and $x_3$ function of a face that
has a neighbouring block or whose axis is periodic ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}), so
`physical` is false exactly on the tangential faces the exchange owns and the slabs there are refreshed; this is
the Cartesian and the spherical-polar case. On the cubed sphere that removal does not run at all — the whole block
is guarded by `type() != "cubed-sphere"` — so every face keeps the function the card named. The cubed-sphere cards
name `custom` on $x_2$ and $x_3$, and `custom_inner` and `custom_outer` are registered built-ins with an empty body
([`bc_func.cpp:7-8`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/68f4e066974ede87e4379285c4fba895b970b7f1/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L7-L8)), so those faces are installed, are not periodic, and `physical` is
true on them: **at the pin no $x_2$ or $x_3$ slab of a cubed-sphere block is refreshed**, and the corners next to a
radial wall keep what the panel exchange left. Nothing writes them instead, because the function that made the face
count as physical does nothing. The radial direction is not split there ($p_z$ is forced to 1,
{{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::_initialize >}}), so every cubed-sphere block
owns both $x_1$ walls and the refresh has something to re-apply; it is the tangential classification, not the
$x_1$ one, that differs.

The check enumerates the rule (`[C19]`).[^cr-c19] Over 35 $(n_g, n_{\mathrm t})$ pairs the two end slabs of width
$n_{\mathrm{slab}}$ never meet, which is what the minimum is for; and over the 140 combinations of
$(n_g, n_{\mathrm t}, \text{tangential face physical}, \text{periodic})$ the number of writers of a corner cell is never more
than one, so the exclusion is exactly what keeps the result independent of the order the bfuncs run in.

[^cr-c19]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C19]`; a Python enumeration of the slab rule of the corner refresh in `src/mesh/meshblock.cpp` at the pin,
    CPU, double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

The refresh runs at the end of every per-stage sync, on `hydro_u` as conserved and on `scalar_s` as scalar, after
both exchanges and before the scalar primitive is rebuilt. It changes only $x_1$ ghost rows inside the tangential ghost
slabs; the one call of a `reflecting` wall also rewrites the other $x_1$ ghost rows, with the values they hold. @fig-ch03-cornerrefresh-wall shows the cells it rewrites.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-cornerrefresh-wall
#| fig-cap: "An $x_1$ wall (thick line) meeting an $x_2$ block seam (dashed purple). The tangential ghost slab (hatched) is filled by the exchange; its cells below the wall (green) are then rewritten by the $x_1$ wall function, so they mirror this side of the seam rather than holding the neighbour's earlier values."
#| fig-alt: "A grid corner where a horizontal wall meets a vertical seam; the ghost cells below the wall on the far side of the seam are highlighted."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.figures.fig_cornerrefresh_wall import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| refresh after the exchange | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}} | `refresh` | none |
| contract of a boundary function | {{< code src/bc/bc_func.hpp BC_FUNCTION >}} | `BC_FUNCTION` | none |

: Code map of the corner refresh. {#tbl-ch03-cornerrefresh-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-cornerrefresh-code):

1. `physical` is true for an installed, non-periodic tangential face ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}).
2. `refresh` loops over the two $x_1$ faces, skips a missing or `is_outflow` function and an $x_1$ axis of one cell,
   and calls the function on each tangential slab whose face is not `physical`, or, for a `reflecting` wall when no
   tangential face is `physical` (`all_owned`), once on the whole array ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}).
3. It runs for `hydro_u` and `scalar_s` with their types ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}} for `refresh`).

**How to use it.** No key: the refresh runs in every per-stage block sync for each installed $x_1$ function except
`outflow`. A user boundary function must honour the `BC_FUNCTION` contract (same ghosts on any slab size). The slab
rule, after the one-call branch of a `reflecting` wall, is ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}):

```cpp
      for (int f = 0; f < nface; ++f) {
        if (!fns[f] || is_outflow(fns[f])) continue;
        ...
          if (any_orth && all_owned && static_cast<size_t>(f) < names.size() &&
              names[f].compare(0, 10, "reflecting") == 0) {
            fns[f](field, spatial, op);
            continue;
          }
        ...
        for (int orth = 1; orth <= 3; ++orth) {
          ...
          int g = ng < n / 2 ? ng : n / 2;
          int inner = (3 - orth) * 2;
          if (!physical(inner)) fns[f](field.narrow(orth, 0, g), spatial, op);
          if (!physical(inner + 1))
            fns[f](field.narrow(orth, n - g, g), spatial, op);
        }
      }
```

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_wb_wall_corner` | a resting polytrope uniform in $x_2$ with viscosity keeps $\max\lvert v_2\rvert/c_s$ and $\max\lvert\mathbf v\rvert/c_s$ small, for the stock wall and a user-named wall | $10^{-12}$ | rest to round-off |
| `test_wb_wall_corner` | a two-block $x_2$ split equals one block | exactly 0 | bitwise |
| `test_wb_wall_corner` | the scalar corner primitive matches its conserved value | exactly 0 | bitwise |

: Tests of the corner refresh. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-cornerrefresh-tests}

The cases are `x2_uniform_rest_keeps_u2_zero` and `user_wall_keeps_u2_zero` ({{< code tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp WallCorner.user_wall_keeps_u2_zero >}}, {{< code tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp WallCorner.x2_uniform_rest_keeps_u2_zero >}}),
`x2_split_matches_one_block_exactly` ({{< code tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp WallCorner.x2_split_matches_one_block_exactly >}}) and
`scalar_corner_primitive_matches_conserved` ({{< code tests/test_wb_wall_corner.cpp WallCorner.scalar_corner_primitive_matches_conserved >}}), each with a `_cuda` twin that
skips without a GPU. One process. They were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).

**Layout coverage.** Every case above declares `layout: slab` with `type: cartesian`, so the rule is asserted on
the Cartesian layout only. It is **untested on the cubed sphere**: no test at the pin asserts a cubed-sphere corner,
which is also where the rule does the least, since `physical` is true on every tangential face there (Derivation).
It is **untested on spherical-polar** as a corner assertion. The spherical-polar path is exercised without being
asserted by `test_x1_centroid_rest_python`, whose deck is reflecting on $x_1$ and $x_2$ and periodic on $x_3$ with
$n_{x_2}=n_{x_3}=4$: the two $x_3$ slabs are refreshed and the two $x_2$ slabs are skipped as physical, and the
test asserts that the column stays at rest, not what the corners hold.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `Mesh::exchange_ghost_zones` does not refresh corners; only the block's per-stage sync does.
- Only $x_1$ walls are refreshed; $x_2$-$x_3$ corners are synthesised (@sec-ch03-exchange).
- On the cubed sphere the rule never fires on a tangential slab: the cards' `custom` faces are installed built-ins,
  so `physical` is true and the radial-wall corners inside the panel halos are left as the exchange wrote them.
:::

The `Mesh`-level sync is a plain exchange ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}} for `exchange_ghost_zones`). A user boundary
function that breaks the contract would write wrong corners without an error (read from the code; not measured). The
switch combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
